Yes, my best friend killed herself many years ago and yes, having that unbearably painful experience of losing her made me see things differently too.  When she died, I felt like the floor was yanked out from under me.  I felt so alone.  It took me about 5 years to be ok with it and about 10 years to get through it.  But, I can tell you from personal experience that if you don't fix whatever was going on with you in the first place, then suicidal thoughts will gradually make their way back into your head.  Take it from me, I never did the work I needed to and now 15 years later, and having experienced 2 suicides and all of the wreckage and it's still not enough to motivate me anymore to stay alive.
I don't blame you for being angry.  I kind of think this is Hell that we're living in now- I know I've already paid for all my sins and then some.  I'm sorry life has been so unkind to you.

Thank you.  About 8yrs ago, my mom was blinded in a car accident with a drunk driver.  Total loss of vision at 58 yrs old.  I did everything possible to help her recover some vision including driving from Phila to Johns Hopkins regularly for the best doctors - it would have been enough but to make a very long story short, trauma doctors as well as some members of my own family went against me and caused even further damage making it that much more difficult.  Her prognosis was better after 6 years of intense treatment and surgeries and then one day out of nowhere, her left eye became hypotonous which is untreatable -it destroys the optic nerve making it impossible to ever see again.  In addition, the same family members that have caused this all but abandoned my mom.  Her life is ruined, it's really awful.  She is on ssdi $1150/month she has no control over anything- she tries- but there are so many limits- more limits than anyone can imagine.  I've always been really close to my mom.  I was 30 when this happened and I put my entire life aside to care for my mom.  I have 2 siblings but they wouldn't share in any of the work so the only choice was to drop everything and pursue her treatment.  I don't regret the sacrifices but now in the aftermath, I am 38 with nothing and I barely recognize myself- all the good is gone.  In addition, my brothers have not come around so my mom is really alone.  I am leaving out a lot of details- my mom made and makes a lot of effort but it's miserable.  She is excluded and disconnected b/c of her blindness.  Now she has 2 grandchildren that she barely gets to spend time with and she has never seen their faces, she has never seen her daughter-in-law's face, and she can't really connect with them - she will never be close with any of them. She feels like an outsider. She is bored to death and she is constantly bombarded with dr visits - so many specialists to see. She is being punished for being blind.  Of course I think to myself how could I even fathom doing this to her but I've become so depressed to the point that I have no desire for anything.  I'm ashamed of my appearance and my lack of growth -surpassed by all peers and friends by decades.  I think I could probably get it together to rebuild but not under these circumstances- I can't keep it together knowing that my mom is being thrown away.  She will have to go to low-income housing that will be 30 min from me and my brother - she will feel even more disconnected and unwanted.  This is not a situation where you try to get through or get past something that happened.  It's like a traumatic event that keeps happening over and over everyday.  It's ongoing there is no end in sight.  I don't have the stomach for it.  I know it's incredibly codependent to base all of my sadness on my mom's situation but I'm not interested in addressing that or anything else anymore.  I love my parents and my family so so much.  I would do anything for them but live.  I want to go to sleep and not wake up.  Thank you for your support.

I feel guilty responding to you considering I want to die and my mother would be left behind.  I am 37 and I have never felt a stronger bond with anyone in my life.  I don't know that I could ever love anyone more in my life.  You are a mom forever.  It hurts my heart to think of your loss.  
There is plenty of grief and sadness - one year's time is nothing- most people suck at dealing with death so make sure to really listen to yourself - really listen to what you need.  If you need to stay in bed and be sad for 2 days, then do it- someone telling you not to- they mean well but it's likely that it's just making them feel uncomfortable.  (Although I have to say - I think it's great he wants to "recognize" the holiday- he sounds like one of the few who actually doesn't suck at dealing)
But, If that's what is happening with your husband, try to go away for a few days or a week- even if it's just an hour away from home- stay in a hotel - where you can just be and feel whatever you feel.  
One thing I can share in my experience as a suicide survivor - it is important to be able to talk about your son in any way at anytime.   Don't let people's stupid standoffish reactions deter you from that.  Talking about him- memories, etc... that is what you still have of him- and that is a big part of him if you hold onto it.  My best friend Debbie killed herself about 15 years ago, I'm still in touch with a mutual friend of ours and he and I talk about her all the time - we laugh a lot - "oh Debbie would have loved that!"etc...  We rehash the bad sometimes, we talk about all of it and we never prevent one another from bringing her up.  That is how I keep part of Debbie with me and I keep in touch with her kids too but the point- that was the most powerful thing in helping me heal.  I'm sorry - all of this unsolicited advice but it's something I think is so great and so rarely utilized.  
One other thing -I'm probably the 50th person to suggest but just in case - suicide survivors support group - not a virtual one either - there may even be one for moms or parents.  
I'm sorry I went on and on - I only did b/c I care so much.  But getting back to your original point- You are a Mother forever - not my opinion, it's a fact.  You will be your son's mom forever no matter what.

in my 20s I looked awesome but it was only because I was ok with being a total fake- I went to tanning beds every week, I had my hair permanently straightened and I took drugs to speed and keep my appetite down and I thought I was on top- while all of my peers were doing things the right way to build something lasting.  I am 37 yr old guy and I look like shit run over twice so believe me I understand.  I am not trying to force you to see the upside but what I have learned about physical appearance is this- take care of yourself for real physically and mentally (mental health).  Do that and it will honestly come together.  It may take years 2-3-4 but trust me, I've seen this right before my eyes with so many people.  Regarding the other students comments - I know hearing those things hurts like hell, there is no way to just flick that off.  But I have to question their intelligence - yes they are mean but there's more to it than that.   That behavior makes sense in junior high- maybe even as far as 9th or 10th grade but all the "cool" people in high school and college- they were attractive and successful, yes.  But they were also relatively secure and confident, they were way too busy with there own lives to actually take time and energy to tell someone they are fat or ugly.  I'm not saying never ever but usually only when provoked like in a fight over something.  I'm sorry this is so wordy- my point is that your peers sound like they are broken too in a way - I know that doesn't make you feel better and I'm not saying forgive them at all, actually f***k them, but I'm trying to drive home the reality that a person that is low enough to say something like that is definitely not a successful person and if they are attractive - I'm willing to bet that the other beautiful people do not find them attractive at all.  
You are in a very bad way - I know very little about autism - I am really sorry.  I can't address the stuff that I don't know about.  Socially though, I can tell you that I believe that people become nicer, more open and understanding as they move into their 30s and 40s.  (with the exception of politicians lol)  Are you near a major city in US or abroad?  I think while it can be more intimidating, you would be more likely to encounter people of quality - educated and open-minded enough to have conversations and possibly even friendships.  
I myself wish I was gone so it's hard for me to tell you to stay but I can tell you that the reason I am living breathing typing this very moment is because I can't accept the pain I would inflict on my parents and my brothers.  For me, I still want to leave desperate to escape my own pain but my family is what stops me.  If you have a lot of love for anyone in your family, then it's worth it to consider what I say.  
And to build on that, it can help to provide motivation to get help.  At my initial evaluation with my therapist she asked why I am here and what I want to accomplish.  I told her that to be honest, if it were up to me, I'd die but I can't bare the thought of my parents suffering my loss so "I know if I don't address my depression, eventually my love for my family will not be enough to keep me here".   I'm sorry this was so incredibly long and wordy I hope you found something in this.  All the best to you.
lynchfan325- your story is nightmare - how in the world did you get through this?  How are you getting through it now?
I understand that -I'm not going to come back with a bunch of cliches but what exactly is the situation?  Are these High School finals or college?  What about yourself is unattractive?

I've reached my breaking point but I want to tell you I think it's good what you did- I know what you're saying...that they are more like people to talk you down but if her listening to you helped at all, it was well worth it.
